subject: Recording window for request vs derived outputs — on-prem pilot Qs
messages:
From: Maya R. <maya@helix.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on what Redwood keeps for on-prem pilot

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. As we prepare the internal security review for our on-prem pilot, a couple of clarifying questions came up around default recording/retention windows for different artifact classes. Can you confirm Redwood's default behavior (and whether it changes for Private/on-prem installs) for the following?

1) Raw user requests (text the customer sends) — stored by default? retention period?
2) Model responses (final generated outputs) — stored by default? retention period?
3) Transient/streamed fragments (partial streaming buffers, intermediate tokens) — ever persisted?
4) Prompt derivatives and indices (embeddings, reranker artifacts, any derived vectors) — where are these kept by default? customer-controlled?
5) KV cache and session state (for multi-turn) — persisted across sessions or flushed?
6) Deletion / purge path: if we request erase for all Helix pilot data, what is the expected timeline and evidence we get?

We're particularly sensitive to whether any of the above are sent to Redwood-hosted services during an on-prem deployment. We can aggregate answers into our questionnaire.

Thanks — attaching our latest security questionnaire to speed things along (see attachment).

Best,
Maya R.
Security Lead | Helix AI

Thanks Maya — good, detailed list. Looping in Karthik and Marissa for technical + compliance specifics; copying Kimberly for contract language if we need to offer an SLA clause.

Short answers up front (high level):
- For Private/on-prem: telemetry that customers opt into can be configured to stay local. By default, our Private installer config sets request/response capture to "disabled" unless you enable it.
- If capture is enabled: defaults differ by artifact class (see Karthik's note that follows).
- Helix's erase requests are supported with documented evidence; typical pipeline 7–30 days depending on dataset size and whether we need a forensic export.

I'll let Karthik enumerate the defaults and exact timelines. Marissa, Kim — please flag if anything below needs legal/compliance framing for Helix's questionnaire.

— Sofia

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Sep 2025 14:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps for on-prem pilot

Hi Maya, Sofia — details below, called out per item. I'll include notes on default config keys for the Private installer so your infra team can review.

1) Raw user requests:
- Private (on-prem): default capture="off". If a customer enables "capture.requests=true" in our operator chart, requests are written to the local flux store and retained according to the configured TTL (default 45 days). No outbound copy is sent to Redwood-hosted control plane unless you opt into "remote-telemetry=true".
- Hosted customers: requests are retained by default for 45 days unless a retention override is requested.

2) Model responses (final outputs):
- Private: similarly controlled by "capture.responses" (default false). If enabled, final outputs are stored locally and follow the same TTL as requests. For compliance, outputs can be marked as "non-persistent" in the config so only ephemeral memory is used.
- Note: both requests and responses can be configured to redact PII with a configurable sanitizer before persistence.

3) Transient/streamed fragments:
- These are not written to durable storage by default. The serving runtime holds streamed buffers in-process and flushes them after the session completes. There is an internal short-lived buffer for streaming (max retention in-memory: a few minutes) but no default persistent capture of partial tokens unless you explicitly enable "capture.stream_fragments=true" (rare).

4) Prompt derivatives & indices (embeddings, reranker vectors):
- By default, embeddings generated through Redwood Optimize or embeddings endpoints are cached in the configured vector store. In Private, the default vector store is local (on-prem). Retention is configurable; out-of-the-box retention is 90 days for derived embeddings unless you provide a custom lifecycle policy.
- These are considered "derived artifacts" and have separate TTLs from raw requests. They can also be put under customer-managed deletion policies.

5) KV cache & session state:
- KV cache is ephemeral by design and is scoped to the serving node/process. Default behavior: caches are in-memory and flushed on pod restart; there's no durable persistence unless the customer enables session-pinning to a persistent store. Session logs (if capture enabled) may include session metadata but not raw KV cache contents unless configured.

6) Deletion / purge path & evidence:
- Erase flow for Private: customer submits an erase request via HubSpot (we'll include HS id). Our operator runs a deletion job that (a) purges local object paths, (b) reconciles vector store deletes, and (c) rotates any temporary credentials. Typical completion: 7–14 days for standard pilot datasets (~<200GB). We provide deletion runbook notes and a signed CSV manifest listing deleted object keys and timestamps. For larger datasets, timeline may extend to 30 days.

Installer config keys (examples):
- capture.requests = false
- capture.responses = false
- capture.stream_fragments = false
- derived_embeddings.ttl_days = 90
- telemetry.remote_telemetry = false

I'll attach a short CSV that maps artifact -> default store -> default TTL for your infra team.

— Karthik

Subject: Re: Questions on what Redwood keeps for on-prem pilot

Hi Maya — a couple compliance notes to add on top of Karthik's technical run-down:

- Evidence of deletion: for Private installs we provide a signed manifest that includes paths/IDs removed and a hash of the exported confirmatory listing. This is what Helix can store as deletion evidence.
- Audit logs: operator-level audit events (who triggered deletion, when) are written to the local audit log by default. If you require external archival, we can integrate with your S3/GCS for exports but that is opt-in.
- SLA/contract language: we can add a clause that states "no Redwood-hosted copies of request/response data will be retained for Private/on-prem deployments unless explicitly enabled and documented." Kimberly, can you prepare a one-paragraph addendum for our draft MSA that says the same and references the TTLs above?

Privacy and PII redaction: we support configurable redaction pipelines before any persistence. If Helix requires default redaction on all captures, we can ship a pre-configured operator profile that sets sanitizer: strict.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks — this is helpful and addresses most of our questions. Couple follow-ups:

- We will require a default sanitizer profile for the pilot (Helix-strict). Can you provide the operator manifest snippet that sets this by default?
- For the deletion manifest: can Redwood include a SHA256 of each deleted object name in the CSV? That eases our evidence ingestion process.

Attaching the questionnaire as Maya's redlines for the SC team — please mark the items you can confirm and we'll feed back the remaining holes.

Best,
Maya

Maya — thanks for the quick responses and the redlined questionnaire. Quick next steps (what I'm attaching / where to look):

1) Operator manifest snippet: included in the Drive link and reproduced below (copy/paste into your helm values):
# Helix-strict sanitizer snippet
telemetry:
  sanitizer:
    profile: strict
    rules:
      - redact_patterns: ["SSN","\u003cPII_EMAIL\u003e"]
      - max_token_length: 512

2) Deletion evidence: we will include a signed CSV with object_id, deletion_timestamp, sha256(object_id) and our operator-run job id. We confirm SHA256 is possible and will be included for Private erasures.

3) Attachments: the redwood_log_schema.csv maps artifacts to default stores and TTLs (from Karthik's note). The security questionnaire you sent is annotated with our answers; I'm attaching the annotated copy (inside the Drive folder).

4) Contract addendum: Kimberly will follow up tomorrow with a one-paragraph MSA addendum; Marissa and I will review.

If you'd like, we can produce a short one-page summary statement suitable for your security team that states: "For Private/on-prem deployments, Redwood does not retain customer request/response data on Redwood-hosted services by default. Any capture to external Redwood services requires explicit customer opt-in and is documented in deployment configuration." Let me know and I'll generate it.

Thanks again — pleased to get this moving.

— Sofia
